[LDET.3.3a.10] **A NaN is not folded.** The compiler must not serialise into
the bundle a compile-time value that is NaN. An expression whose value at compile
time is NaN is lowered as written, and the engine evaluates it ([LDET.3.6.2]).
IEEE 754 leaves a NaN's sign and payload to the hardware ([LEXP.4.3]), so a
folded NaN would make the bundle's bytes depend on the compiler host, which
[LDET.3.3a.7] forbids. `+Inf` and `-Inf` each have one encoding and fold like any
other value.
